messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Genetic map of the X chromosome
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl2-disc] Genetic map of the X chromosome
messages.body_plain:
The sex-averaged and male cM positions are left as missing for the X chromosome, and only the female cM positions are provided.
So you need to pull out the female positions for the X chromosome and the average positions for the autosomes.

Physical map positions of the CC/DO founder SNPs are available in a SQLite database, built from the Sanger sequencing data.
See https://kbroman.org/qtl2/pages/move_to_build39.html

The genetic map positions in mmconvert are obtained by interpolation of positions in the Cox map, https://github.com/kbroman/CoxMapV3

karl

> However, all the rsIDs located in the X chromosome produce a 'NA' value in the genetic map.
>
> Is there any particular reason behind this or am I missing something?
> Are there any available physical and genetic map datasets for all the founder SNPs?
>

messages.subject: Converting file to R/qtl2 format
messages.body_plain:
Dear R/qtl users,

I am attempting to perform a QTL analysis from a VCF file.  Currently, I have created two CSV files using suggestions from a previous thread.  One file is an SNP matrix with marker genotypes, and the other has marker name, chromosome, and position.

Is there an easy way to make these files into one that is acceptable for the R/qtl2 package?  I am very new to QTL and would appreciate any help in this regard.

Thanks,
Eric

messages.subject: Re: Converting file to R/qtl2 format
messages.body_plain:
I’m not sure about “easy”.

The input file format is described at https://kbroman.org/qtl2/assets/vignettes/input_files.html

There are sample data files at https://kbroman.org/qtl2/pages/sampledata.html
as well as at https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2data

The latter includes, in many cases, R scripts to prepare the data files.
For example, see https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2data/blob/main/BXD/R/convertData.R

karl
